links.outcome: Expert-rated clinical accuracy, patient safety, and faithfulness with versus without retrieval grounding
links.effect: RAG improved Qwen3 accuracy (+0.44, P<0.001) but not DeepSeek (+0.21, P=0.09); safety showed no reliable benefit; faithfulness fell on Qwen3 (-0.24, P<0.001).
links.quote: RAG produced no stable, consistent improvement across the three content-quality dimensions ( Table 2 and Figure 3 ).

links.outcome: Existence of retrieved PubMed identifiers verified against PubMed
links.effect: All retrieved PMIDs existed in PubMed (236 question-level instances, 187 unique; 100% existence rate, zero fabricated references), though existence did not establish relevance or support.
links.quote: All PMIDs retrieved by the RAG arm existed in PubMed (236 question-level instances, 187 unique; 100% existence rate, zero fabricated references).

links.outcome: Clinical knowledge accuracy and safety on high-difficulty perioperative IBD questions, including contraindications
links.effect: On DeepSeek, RAG received failing safety scores (≤2) on six high-risk questions; Q34 RAG safety 1.00 versus baseline 3.67 with off-topic retrieved evidence.
links.quote: Moreover, on DeepSeek, RAG received failing safety scores (≤2) on six high-risk questions ( Table 3 ) (epidural drug combinations, sedative identification, drug interactions), indicating that retrieval failed to prevent—and sometimes accompanied—unsafe outputs in high-risk scenarios.

links.outcome: Output accuracy and safety against guideline-based expert judgment
links.effect: Mean accuracy was 2.85 (RAG) vs 2.64 (baseline) on DeepSeek and 3.64 vs 3.20 on Qwen3; safety did not reliably improve and unsafe outputs persisted.
links.quote: Authentic retrieved sources could still accompany incorrect or unsafe outputs, demonstrating that evidence traceability and clinical reliability are distinct dimensions.

links.outcome: Whether the model abstained when retrieved evidence was insufficient
links.effect: For Q34, the RAG response acknowledged snippets were not directly relevant but still generated a specific, unsafe recommendation (safety 1.00 vs baseline 3.67).
links.quote: At the same time, the model did not recognize the insufficiency of the available evidence and abstain, but generated a specific clinical recommendation from off-target information.

links.outcome: Deployed local RAG configuration performance on high-difficulty intended-use perioperative IBD questions
links.effect: Retrieval did not consistently improve accuracy, safety or faithfulness across the two deployed 8B model configurations.
links.quote: In the two evaluated 8B models, using the present 50-question benchmark and IBD-anchored retrieval corpus, PubMed-based retrieval achieved source-existence authenticity but did not consistently improve clinical accuracy, safety, or faithfulness.

unlisted_practices: Separating source-existence verification from clinical correctness evaluation in RAG
Model-external deterministic safety rule layer for high-risk drugs (proposed, not tested)

screen.reason: The study evaluates whether adding retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) to existing models improves clinical accuracy, patient safety, and faithfulness compared to matched no-retrieval conditions.
